posts.title: Tapestries and harmonies: visualizing lyrics
posts.description: From rap tapestries to type harmonies, this post asks how visualization can make rhyme, rhythm, timing, and vocal harmony visible. Experiments with duets, K-pop, and rounds reveal both the expressive potential and limits of typography. These emergent visualizations point toward harder, less-structured data as the next frontier for visual analytics. Continue reading →

posts.title: Abstraction vs. realism in visualization
posts.description: How abstract should a visualization be? I consider Saharan et al's new multi-dimensional design space for representational fidelity, consider various trade-offs, and applicability to text and broader data visualization. Continue reading →
